I'll think this through as old Wang would — same as every year, with small adjustments.

---

I am 76 years old now, been working this land 50 years. My back is not what it was, but my two sons help when they come back from town, and my wife still does plenty. 16 mu is not small, not big — manageable for our family.

This year I do the same as last year, mostly. Why change? What worked, worked. Wheat goes in after maize harvest in October, then maize goes in right after wheat comes off in June. Same as always on this plain.

**For my wheat:**
I will use the improved seed I bought from the same dealer in town — everyone in our village uses similar variety, gives good harvest if the spring rain comes. I plant about 15 kg seed per mu, a bit thick because some seed always fails.

For fertilizer, before planting I spread two bags of compound fertilizer per mu — that is the 15-15-15 kind, 50 kg bag, so 100 kg compound. Then in spring at jointing time, I broadcast one bag of urea per mu, about 25-30 kg, together with the spring water. That gives the wheat strength to make grain. My neighbor Old Liu tried less urea two years ago and his yield dropped — I will not make that mistake. Better to spend a few yuan more than lose 50 kg of grain.

Water: I give winter water before freezing, then jointing water in spring, then one more around heading time. Three irrigations, sometimes four if April is dry. The well still pumps fine.

Spray: weeds in early spring once, aphids around flowering once, maybe wheat scab spray if the weather turns warm and wet — so two or three times. I cannot afford to lose the crop to bugs.

Plough the field after maize comes off, then harrow and plant. That is how it has always been done.

I expect maybe 500 kg per mu wheat. Last year was about that.

**For my summer maize:**
Right after wheat harvest, no time to plough — I just plant directly with the seeder, no-till. Saves time and the soil keeps moisture. Hybrid seed, the dealer recommends one variety each year, I trust him, been buying from him 20 years.

Base fertilizer: I put one and a half bags of compound at planting, about 75 kg per mu. Then when the maize is knee-high I topdress one bag of urea, 25 kg per mu. If the leaves look pale I add a little more — maize tells you when it is hungry.

Water: usually one or two times if July-August is dry. Rain is better but the well is there if needed.

Spray: once for armyworm or borer, sometimes a second time. Two sprays usually.

Maize yield maybe 550 kg per mu, sometimes more if the rain is good.
